newsitem.title: USA: Dow ends above 7,000 milestone for first time.
newsitem.headline: Dow ends above 7,000 milestone for first time.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average closed above 7,000 points for the first time Thursday as the stock market rode a wave of investor confidence based on low interest rates and non-inflationary economic growth.

The Dow ended up 60.81 points, or 0.87 percent, at an all-time high of 7,022.44, beating the previous record set just Wednesday. The rally capped a breathtaking run that has added 1,000 points to the blue-chip index in just four months.

The Standard & Poor's composite and NYSE Composite indexes also set new highs. In the broader market, advancing issues swamped declines 1,717 to 820 on very heavy volume of 584 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
Early in the session, the Dow staged a series of brief forays above 7,000 but failed to mount a serious charge until the recently dormant bond market sprang to life.

"This market is interpreting everything positively right now," said Charlie Crane, director of research at Spears Benzak Salomon & Farrell. "Today, all of a sudden the bond market got its legs and pretty soon, stocks were dancing."

The bond rally, which began just after the U.S. Treasury sold $10.0 billion in bonds in a quarterly auction, lifted the bellwether 30-year Treasury bond nearly a full point, which reduced its yield to 6.63 percent from 6.71 percent on Wednesday.
Stoking the demand for stocks is a strong dollar, analysts said, citing a variety of reasons that the currency's recent rise has lifted the market.

"The dollar's strength is diminshing fears of inflation because a strong dollar tends to lower the cost of imports," said Jack Shaughnessy, director of research at Advest. "Clearly, inflation has always been a critical variable for the market."
Another by-product is renewed international demand for U.S. financial assets.

While the favourable economic backdrop remained intact, stocks still needed evidence of continued corporate earnings growth to sustain their rally. The just-concluded wave of fourth-quarter results provided that, analysts said.

"There are two things that matter, interest rates and corporate earnings," said Phil Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line Asset Management. "Rates are coming down and corporate earnings are still showing powerful growth."
Even with all the elements of a positive market environment in place, several analysts warned that the bull market seems to be developing a cult of personality.

"People are starting to treat these top 50 stocks as collectors' items," said Richard Cripps, chief market strategist at Legg Mason Wood Walker. "We need to enjoy this but not necessarily take on more risk at these levels."
Merrill Lynch & Co. led a sharp rally in financial stocks. The shares, which were added to Goldman Sachs' recommended list, jumped 8-1/2 to 86-1/2.
Citicorp rose four to 123-1/2 and BankAmerica Corp. gained 5-1/8 to 123.
Pharmaceutical shares were also strong. Merck & Co. rose 3-3/4 to 99-5/8 and Pfizer Inc. rose 2-3/8 to 96. Johnson & Johnson gained 1-1/8 to 61-3/4 after A.G. Edwards upgraded the shares.
The Nasdaq Composite index rose 11.85 points to 1,370.81.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 9.05 to 811.82, a new high. The American Stock Exchange index rose 2.30 to 595.40.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks rose 4.54 points to 424.42, a new high. The average share was up 47 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was at a new high of 7,757.389, up 78.736, or 1.03 percent.
